title: The Boy Who Went to the North Wind and Demanded His Meal Back
placement: Each illustration belongs directly after the paragraph with index "paragraph" (0-based, paragraphs split on blank lines).

cover.caption: The boy went straight to the North Wind to demand his meal back.
cover.alt: The boy leans into the gale on a steep mountain path. Ahead of him the North Wind fills the sky, blowing snow straight at him.
cover.prompt: On a steep, windswept path high on a bare fell, the Boy leans hard into the gale with his fists clenched and his long scarf streaming out behind him, not giving an inch. Ahead of him the huge face of the North Wind fills the grey sky, cheeks puffed out and bushy eyebrows bristling, blowing a flurry of snow straight at him. The few trees on the slope all lean the same way.

Create the cover illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: On a steep, windswept path high on a bare fell, the Boy leans hard into the gale with his fists clenched and his long scarf streaming out behind him, not giving an inch. Ahead of him the huge face of the North Wind fills the grey sky, cheeks puffed out and bushy eyebrows bristling, blowing a flurry of snow straight at him. The few trees on the slope all lean the same way.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Boy: A small, skinny boy of about eleven with a narrow, pale face, cheeks reddened by the cold, big sticking-out ears, bright blue eyes, a stubborn little frown and white-blond hair that sticks up in tufts. He wears a grey knitted jumper several sizes too big, patched dark-brown trousers, thick grey socks, heavy scuffed boots and a long brown knitted scarf wound twice round his neck.
- the North Wind: A huge, grumbling old man made of swirling white and pale-grey cloud, with no legs, only a long, whirling tail of mist and snowflakes. He has a broad, weathered face with puffed-out round cheeks, icy-blue eyes, great bushy white eyebrows, a thick moustache like drifted snow and a long, frosty white beard that streams away in the wind, and big, soft hands of cloud. Snowflakes and tiny icicles glitter in his tangled white hair.

Story world: Old rural Norway at the first frost of late autumn. The boy and his mother live in a small, grey, weathered log cottage with a turf roof; beside it stands a little storehouse on posts with a steep wooden stair up to its door. Far to the north, on a bare, windswept fell where every tree leans south, stands the North Wind's house, a low, crooked log house with a sod roof weighed down with stones. On the road between them lies the inn, a big, low log house with a lantern at the door and a goat shed behind. The meal is carried in a grey sack. The magic cloth is a square white linen tablecloth with a red woven zigzag border, and the swapped one looks exactly the same. The stick is a knobbly old stick of pale birch wood, about as long as the boy is tall.

This story's season, light and colours: Blustery late autumn at the first frost: rimed grass and bare birches, cold blue-grey skies with fast, torn clouds, and snow already lying on the northern fells where the North Wind lives. Indoors, warm firelight and glowing embers against cold blue windows. Accents: flour white, lingonberry red and pewter grey.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. characters.name: The Boy
characters.description: A determined, practical youth who refuses to accept being robbed and is brave enough to demand justice from the North Wind.
characters.look: A small, skinny boy of about eleven with a narrow, pale face, cheeks reddened by the cold, big sticking-out ears, bright blue eyes, a stubborn little frown and white-blond hair that sticks up in tufts. He wears a grey knitted jumper several sizes too big, patched dark-brown trousers, thick grey socks, heavy scuffed boots and a long brown knitted scarf wound twice round his neck.

characters.name: The Old Mother
characters.description: Poor and frail, she depends on her son for food and doubts miracles until she sees them with her own eyes.
characters.look: A thin, frail old woman of about sixty-five, a little stooped, with a long, gentle, deeply lined face, tired grey eyes, a thin mouth and one eyebrow often raised in doubt. Her grey hair hangs in one thin braid over her shoulder. She wears a faded plum-coloured homespun dress, a darned brown knitted shawl, a long patched linen apron and wooden clogs.

characters.name: The North Wind
characters.description: A blunt, powerful force given a voice and a home, both feared and strangely fair when confronted directly.
characters.look: A huge, grumbling old man made of swirling white and pale-grey cloud, with no legs, only a long, whirling tail of mist and snowflakes. He has a broad, weathered face with puffed-out round cheeks, icy-blue eyes, great bushy white eyebrows, a thick moustache like drifted snow and a long, frosty white beard that streams away in the wind, and big, soft hands of cloud. Snowflakes and tiny icicles glitter in his tangled white hair.

characters.name: The Innkeeper
characters.description: A greedy schemer who tries to swap magical treasures for worthless lookalikes and is finally forced to return what he stole.
characters.look: A tall, gangly innkeeper of about fifty with a long, narrow face, a much too wide, toothy smile, small glittering eyes, a long pointed chin and oily black hair twisted into one big curl on his forehead. He wears a wine-red waistcoat with shiny brass buttons over a white linen shirt with rolled sleeves, a long blue-and-white striped apron, dark breeches and a wide black leather money belt that jingles with coins.

characters.name: The Billy-Goat
characters.description: A seemingly ordinary goat gifted by the North Wind, enchanted to produce gold ducats on command.
characters.look: A small, sturdy billy goat about the size of a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail and neat black hooves. Around his neck he wears a red leather collar hung with two small brass bells.

places.name: the Inn Parlour
places.look: A big, low-ceilinged parlour in an old log inn, with dark, smoke-stained timber walls, a large open fireplace, two long plank tables with benches, a small corner table under a frosted window, an iron lantern hanging from a beam, pewter mugs on a shelf and a heavy plank door to the frosty yard. Warm, smoky and golden.

- the Billy Goat: A small, sturdy billy goat about the size of a large dog, with a shaggy snow-white coat, a light-grey face with a little pointed grey beard, bright amber eyes with slot-shaped pupils, short, curved, ridged horns, a stubby tail and neat black hooves.
